extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers for Elsevier journals (academic manuscript reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Checklist and guidance for reviewers assessing submitted manuscripts for Elsevier journals, covering whether to accept a review, confidentiality, evaluation criteria for original and review articles, additional reporting/ethics considerations, and how to finalize constructive reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify expertise aligns with article scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify expertise aligns with article scope
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before accepting a review, confirm that the manuscript falls within your domain of expertise so you can competently assess its content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose potential conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declare any financial, personal, or professional conflicts that might bias your review before accepting the assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confirm availability to meet deadlines
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure you have the time to complete a thorough review within the journal's requested timeframe; decline if you cannot meet deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review peer review process fundamentals
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Familiarize yourself with the journal's peer review workflow and what is expected of reviewers (e.g., confidentiality, format of comments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Familiarize yourself with reviewer policies
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read the journal/publisher reviewer policies (ethical standards, confidentiality, authorship, data policies) before accepting the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat manuscripts as 'confidential documents' and do not share with anyone without editor authorization
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not upload manuscript content to generative AI tools; never disclose peer review information; only share manuscript material if explicitly authorized by the editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title accuracy and discoverability (original research)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the title accurately reflects the content and is likely to make the work discoverable to the appropriate audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract completeness and clarity (original research)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the abstract succinctly summarizes objectives, methods, key results, and conclusions and is clear to readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction's background and objectives (original research)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that the introduction provides sufficient background, frames the gap in knowledge, and states clear objectives or hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods sufficiency for replication (original research)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether the methods are described in enough detail for another researcher to reproduce the experiments or analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results presentation and statistical reporting (original research)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess clarity and completeness of results, including appropriate use and reporting of statistical analyses, figures, tables, and data presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion support from data (original research)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the interpretations and conclusions in the discussion are adequately supported by the presented data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference currency and relevance (original research)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that citations are up-to-date and relevant, and that the literature review accurately situates the work in context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language quality and readability (original research)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comment on clarity, grammar, and overall readability; identify if language issues impede understanding and whether editing is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novel or important contributions (original research)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the study makes a clear, novel, or significant contribution to the field and whether claims are justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical and integrity concerns (original research)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag any issues relating to ethics, consent, animal welfare, data integrity, plagiarism, or falsification; raise such suspicions to the editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance justification (review articles)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For review articles, assess whether the review's scope is clearly justified and timely for the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical development coverage (review articles)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the review appropriately covers the historical development and evolution of the topic where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference comprehensiveness (review articles)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that references are comprehensive and balanced, avoiding major omissions or biased citation practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological transparency (review articles)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess transparency of the review methods (e.g., how sources were selected, inclusion/exclusion criteria) where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical method appropriateness (review articles)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If review includes quantitative synthesis or meta-analysis, evaluate whether statistical methods are appropriate and correctly applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall structure and clarity (review articles)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether the review is well-organized, logically structured, and communicates key points clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language quality (review articles)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess grammar, style, and readability for review articles and whether editorial improvement is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sex and gender reporting practices
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether authors have reported sex and gender appropriately where relevant to the research design, analysis, and interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research data and visualization quality
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the quality, clarity, and appropriateness of data presentation and visualizations (figures, tables, charts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical approval documentation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify that required ethical approvals, permits, or consent documentation are provided or appropriately referenced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summarize the article briefly (finalizing review)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin the review with a concise summary of the manuscript to demonstrate understanding and provide context for comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide specific, constructive feedback
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give actionable suggestions for improvement, point to exact locations in the manuscript, and avoid vague criticisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use clear paragraph structure in review
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize comments into clear paragraphs or sections (e.g., major issues, minor issues) to improve readability and utility to authors/editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check conformity to journal guidelines
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the manuscript follows the target journal's formatting, reporting, and submission requirements and flag nonconformity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Raise plagiarism or falsification suspicions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you suspect plagiarism, data fabrication, or falsification, report these concerns privately to the editor with supporting evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider unconscious bias
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflect on potential unconscious biases in your assessment and avoid letting them unduly influence recommendations or tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't focus on minor spelling issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't focus on minor spelling issues
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid making the review about trivial copyediting items; focus on substantive scientific or scholarly issues unless language impedes understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't make personal attacks
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep critiques professional and avoid derogatory or ad hominem remarks about authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't dismiss alternative viewpoints
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be open to legitimate alternative interpretations or methods and critique them on scientific grounds rather than dismissing them out of hand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't share reviews without authorization
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain confidentiality: do not disseminate reviewer reports or manuscript content unless the editor has authorized sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't self-promote citations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid recommending citations primarily to increase your own citation count; suggest citations only if they genuinely improve the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation options
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation Options: Reject; Accept without revision; Revise (major or minor)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Based on your assessment, choose the appropriate recommendation option and justify your decision with specific reasons and required changes where applicable.
